title: WPSS/1277/2020 of HARGOVIND UPADHYAY Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No.1277 of 2020
Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.

Mr. K.P. Upadhyaya, Senior Advocate,
assisted by Mr. Hem ant Pant, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Additional C.S.C. for
the State of Uttarakhand.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Petitioner was appointed as Assistant
Teacher in a recognized Senior Basic
School, after due approval of the Com petent
Authority. Subsequently, the said school
was included in the grant-in-aid list.
Consequently, petitioner started getting
salary from public exchequer. According to
the petitioner, he was entitled to benefit of
tim e scale, which is adm issible to other
Teachers serving in a Governm ent Aided
I nstitution, upon com pletion of 10 years of
satisfactory service on the sam e post.
Thus, according to him , since he was
appointed as Assistant Teacher on
14.02.1992, therefore, he is entitled to
selection grade of pay w.e.f. 14.02.2002.
I n this writ petition, petitioner has
sought the following reliefs:
"(a) To issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus directing the respondents to
grant the benefit of time scale to the Petitioner after
computing 10 years of service from the date of his
initial appointment i.e. 14/ 02/ 1992 and release the
arrears of the pecuniary benefits as a result of re-fixation of the salary, as the case of the Petitioner is
squarely covered by the by the Judgment of this
Hon'ble Court dated 27/ 03/ 2017 passed in Writ
Petition (S/ S) No. 1655 of 2015, Harish Singh Bora
and others v/ s State of Uttarakhand and others,
which has attained finality.
(b) To issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus Directing the respondents to
release/ pay to the Petitioner his Pension and other
retiral benefits by taking into consideration his
entire length of service from the date of his initial

appointment i.e. 14/ 02/ 1992.
(c) To issue a writ of Mandamus directing the
respondents to pay an interest at the rate of 9% per
annum on the arrears that have occurred due to the
non payment of admissible salary, Pension and
other retiral benefits to the Petitioner."
The order passed by District Basic
Education Officer, Nainital on 13/ 14-02-
1992, granting approval for appointing the
petitioner, is on record as Annexure No. 1.
Perusal of the record, however, indicates
that petitioner was actually appointed by
Manager vide order dated 20.02.1992 and
he joined duties as Assistant Teacher in
Adarsh I nter College, Sanjay Nagar,
Bindukhatta, Lalkuan, on 27.02.1992. I t is
not in dispute that the institution, in which
petitioner was appointed, was not getting
any financial aid at the tim e of petitioner's
appointm ent; although, the said institution
was duly recognized by the Com petent
Authority. Token grant of ` 1,00,000/ - was
sanctioned to the aforesaid institution vide
Governm ent Order dated 24.05.2005 and,
thereafter, vide Governm ent Order dated
03.03.2007, the aforesaid institution was
included in the grant-in-aid list of the State
Governm ent.
Petitioner has relied upon a
Governm ent Order dated 15.07.1999 for
contending that salary of Teachers/
em ployees of recognized schools, which
were subsequently included in the grant-in-aid list of the State, has to be fixed after
taking into account entire length of their
service from the date of their initial
appointm ent.
Learned Senior Advocate for the
petitioner thus subm its that the service
rendered by petitioner as Assistant Teacher
in the institution in question, before its
inclusion in grant-in-aid list, cannot be
ignored and, as such, petitioner is entitled
to selection grade upon com pletion of 10
years of service from the date of his initial

appointm ent.
Learned Senior Advocate for the
petitioner has placed reliance upon
judgm ent dated 27.03.2017 rendered by
Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in WPSS
No. 1955 of 2015 and other connected
petitions. He, thus, subm its that identical
controversy was involved in the said writ
petition also, therefore, the present writ
petition deserves to be allowed in term s of
the said judgm ent. Learned Senior Advocate
further points out that the judgm ent
rendered in WPSS No. 1955 of 2015 was
affirm ed by Division Bench of this Court and
S.L.P. filed by State against the judgm ent
rendered by Division Bench of this Court too
was dism issed. Subsequently, a Review
Petition was filed by the State, which was
also dism issed by Hon'ble Suprem e Court.
Learned State Counsel although do not
dispute the subm ission m ade on behalf of
the petitioner that identical issue has been
decided by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court
in the aforesaid writ petition, however, he
refers to a Governm ent Order dated
06.09.2019 for contending that benefit of
selection grade would be adm issible to
Teachers of recognized schools only after 10
years from the date of inclusion of such
recognized school in the grant-in-aid list of
the State Governm ent.
This subm ission m ade by learned
State Counsel is unacceptable for the sim ple
reason that no person can be divested of his
vested or accrued right by an executive
instruction. Teachers serving in recognized
schools, which were later included in grant-in-aid list, acquired certain rights under the
then existing Governm ent Policy. Those
rights got crystalized by the judgm ent
rendered by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court
in favour of Teachers of recognized schools,
wherein it was held that they are entitled to
selection grade upon com pletion of 10 years
of satisfactory service, to be reckoned from

the date of their initial appointm ent. Such
vested or accrued right cannot be taken
away by a Governm ent Order, which is in
the nature of executive instruction.
Section 6 of the General Clauses Act
provides the effect of repeal of a Legislation
and, clause (c) thereof, ordains that repeal
of a Legislation shall not affect any right,
privilege, obligation or liability acquired,
accrued or incurred under any enactm ent so
repealed.
The opening paragraph of Governm ent
Order dated 06.09.2019 reveals that it is
applicable only to such Teachers, who were
serving on the date of issuance of the said
Governm ent Order. Petitioner retired from
service m uch before issuance of the
Governm ent Order, on 30.03.2018,
therefore, the stipulation m ade in the
Governm ent Order will not have any
application to the petitioner.
Even otherwise also, declaration of a
right in favour of Teachers serving in
recognized institutions by this Court cannot
be set at naugt by the State by issuing
executive instruction.
Since the controversy has been
decided in favour of Teachers of recognized
institutions by Co-ordinate Bench of this
Court, the present writ petition also
deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, the writ petition is
allowed, the respondent no. 2 is directed to
sanction and release benefit of tim e scale to
the petitioner from due date, after taking
into account his entire length of service,
within a period of eight weeks' from the
date of production of certified copy of this
order. I t is, however, provided that if
paym ent is not released within eight weeks,
then petitioner shall be entitled to interest
@ 9% per annum .
I t is m ade clear that this Court has not
exam ined petitioner's entitlem ent for
pension under old schem e. Therefore,

petitioner shall be at liberty to approach the
Com petent Authority for adjudication of his
right for pension under the old schem e.

( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.)
 14.03.2023
Arpan
